Both panes should fail with a confusing internal-looking diagnostic rather
than the compile succeeding or naming the actual problem (an uninitialized
index used to subscript a structured-buffer array member). Look at the exit
status and the first line of stderr, not at whether disassembly appears.
CE's Linux builds drop the `llvm::` qualifier that the local Windows Debug
build prints, but it is the same underlying failure: dxc_1_6_2112 exits 29
(the low byte of the DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR HRESULT) printing "Internal
Compiler error: cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!"; dxc_trunk exits 5
(the low byte of E_FAIL) printing "error: cast<X>() argument of incompatible
type!" -- reworded by an unrelated driver change between the two builds, not
a fix. CE runs Release builds, so this corroborates the local Debug ground
truth's LLVM-assert signature; it does not independently date anything older
than 1.6.2112.
